memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make a curtain of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, with cherubim woven into it by a skilled worker. Hang it with gold hooks on four posts of acacia wood overlaid with gold and standing on four silver bases. Hang the curtain from the clasps and place the ark of the covenant law behind the curtain. The curtain will separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place." - Exodus 26:31-33 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This curtain had one purpose: to separate. It hung between the Holy Place and the Most Holy Place, marking a boundary that could not be casually crossed. Behind it sat the ark, and above the ark, God's presence. The woven cherubim were a visual reminder — like the angels guarding Eden's entrance, they signalled that the way in was closed.

That curtain preached a hard truth every single day. A holy God and a sinful people cannot simply mingle. Only the high priest passed through, only once a year, and never without blood. The message was unmistakable: there is a barrier, and you cannot remove it yourself.

Which makes what happened at Calvary so staggering. At the moment Jesus died, the temple curtain was torn in two from top to bottom (Matt 27:51) — torn downward, from God's side, by God's hand. The barrier that no one could cross was opened by the death of Christ. Hebrews says we now enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus, through a new and living way opened for us through the curtain, that is, His body (Heb 10:19-20). What stood closed for centuries stands open for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I live in the full freedom of a way that has been opened for me?
What does it mean that God tore the curtain from His side, not ours?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, the barrier I could never remove, You tore open Yourself through Christ. Thank You that the way into Your presence stands open. Let me come with confidence and gratitude. Amen.
